title: Other Callenders: Howard and Charles Callender
summary: Willard asks if trumpeters Howard and Charles Callender were relatives; Callender met Charles at Cafe Society.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: ...a couple of other Callenders I ran across. One is Howard Callender, who played trumpet with Eddie Diaz(?) and his Boston Brownies in 1931. You mentioned your family having lived in Boston. I wondered if Howard Callender was any relation of yours.
Well, all the Callenders come from Barbados originally, so...
Yes. So he is probably a distant relative. That's from before me. 1931. Howard.
But I wondered if you were aware of him, or...
No, I wasn't aware of him, but I am aware of Charles Callender. He's a trumpet player. I met him.
And I understand he worked with and recorded with Nat Cole in 1939. Someone told me that, I believe. I don't think I could find that in a discography.
It must have been in New York. I don't think he's ever been out here.
But you say you met him?
Yes, I met him when I was in New York, when I was a kid. Well, not exactly a kid, but in the Forties when I was working in the Cafe Society with Lee and Lester's band.
And did you try to establish whether or not you were related?
No, we didn't really set any firm tie. But since all Callenders come from the one island mostly, we figured that we had to be related somehow.
